Native artwork history grammar reconstructed from the two configured Windows PE images.
This is source reconstruction, not a test, acceptance report, or observed game result.
Reference SHA-256: 205770918fd54c96cbbcf89223ebd449e2e113c7c873ed81177c4511a3450db7
Classic SHA-256: f35bbaf37aa96f93f95f8a35a9341e6649da46bc29a8650316bfdc2dfc57f3e4

Coordinates and complete source:
  native-rtti-dispatch.tsv reads every concrete history_event*st RTTI/COL/vtable.
  Each edition has 133 event roots at slot +0xd8 and 18 collection roots at +0x30.
  *-event-source-call-closure.tsv preserves the actual reachable literal operands,
  direct calls, conditional switch context, normalized selectors, and indirect edges.
  *-event-source-call-closure.asm preserves the actual complete bodies. Embedded
  switch data printed as instructions by objdump must be interpreted with the TSV.
  Dynamic RAW/entity/name fields remain explicit typed leaves rather than invented
  full sentences. Item title virtuals continue into the existing complete native
  item-info-title/item-raw-title and statue-art source catalogues.

===============================================================================
ART_IMAGE PARAGRAPH HISTORY SUFFIX
Reference 0x1451b10..0x145312c; Classic 0x144ca80..0x144e09c
Reference history suffix 0x1452a20..0x1452b99;
Classic history suffix 0x144d990..0x144db09.
===============================================================================

void append_history_suffix(art_image *image, string &out,
                           bool full_description, bool english_name_gloss) {
    if (!full_description) return; // also skips symbol/commission suffix
    if (image->event == -1) goto symbol_and_commission;
    history_event *event = find_event(image->event);
    if (!event) goto symbol_and_commission;
    out += "The artwork relates to ";
    history_context ctx;
    if (english_name_gloss) ctx.flags |= 2;
    out += event->virtual_0xd8(ctx, true, false); // all 133 concrete roots

    // Reverse whole collection vector, and stop at the first containing the ID.
    // The native collection's event_ids are searched through helper 0x0babe0.
    for (int i = history.collections.size() - 1; i >= 0; --i) {
        history_event_collection *collection = history.collections[i];
        if (find_id(collection->event_ids, event->id) != -1) {
            out += " during ";
            out += collection->virtual_0x30(); // all 18 concrete roots
            break;
        }
    }
    out += ".  ";
symbol_and_commission:
    // Original art_image function continues into symbol/commission only when
    // specific_ref.type == 24 and its entity and art_image_types index resolve.
    // Category 0: "The image is the symbol of "; category 1:
    // "The image was commissioned by ". Both use the full eleven-way entity
    // switch, preserved in statue-art-sources.tsv and this edition's art ASM.
}

===============================================================================
SHARED DATE BUILDER
Reference 0xb92640..0xb928f4; Classic 0xb8f680..0xb8f934
===============================================================================

// Integer multiplication/shift in the assembly implements signed / 100800.
// Only tick == -1 suppresses season precision. No text callback is involved.
void append_date(string &out, int year, int tick) {
    if (year < 1) { out += "a time before time"; return; }
    string year_text = signed_decimal(year); // Reference 0x52c2b0
    if (tick == -1) { out += year_text; return; }
    out += "the ";
    int season = trunc_toward_zero(tick / 100800);
    int within_season = tick - season * 100800;
    if (within_season > 67200) out += "late ";
    else if (within_season <= 33600) out += "early ";
    else out += "mid";
    switch (season) {
    case 0: out += "spring"; break;
    case 1: out += "summer"; break;
    case 2: out += "autumn"; break;
    case 3: out += "winter"; break;
    default: break; // native malformed/out-of-year tick: no season noun
    }
    out += " of "; // native inline DWORD immediate 0x20666f20
    out += year_text;
}

// Four seasons x three thirds: the early spring / midspring / late spring,
// the early summer / midsummer / late summer, the early autumn / midautumn /
// late autumn, the early winter / midwinter / late winter, each " of YEAR".
// These twelve + YEAR + a time before time are the fourteen ordinary outputs.
// The native default still appends phase and year when season is outside 0..3;
// the ASM records that branch instead of assigning it an invented season.

===============================================================================
ADD HISTORICAL FIGURE -> ENTITY LINK SUBJECT: ALL 16 SELECTORS AND DEFAULT
Reference 0xb80420..0xb80ad4; Classic 0xb7d460..0xb7db14
First table Reference 0xb80a54; second table 0xb80a94.
===============================================================================

// Native parameters: event+0x28 entity ID; +0x2c figure ID; +0x30 selector;
// +0x34 position ID; +0x08 year; +0x0c tick. Native context enters shared names.
void entity_link_subject(event *e, string &out, context *ctx) {
    position *p;
    switch (e->selector) {
    case 0: out += "the acceptance"; break;
    case 1: case 3: case 5: case 7: case 13: out += "the status"; break;
    case 2: out += "the entry"; break;
    case 4: out += "the enslavement"; break;
    case 6: out += "the imprisonment"; break;
    case 8: out += "the rise"; break;
    case 9: out += "the crimes"; break;
    case 10:
        p = find_entity_position(e->entity, e->position);
        if (!p) break; // common actor/entity/date continuation still runs
        unsigned flags0 = p->flags.bytes.empty() ? 0 : p->flags.bytes[0];
        if (flags0 & 0x40 || !p->succession_by_position.empty())
            out += "the ascension";
        else if (!p->appointed_by.empty()) out += "the appointment";
        else if (flags0 & 0x02) out += "the election";
        else out += "the selection";
        break;
    case 12:
        if (find_entity_position(e->entity, e->position)) out += "the claim";
        break;
    case 15: out += "the work"; break;
    case 11: case 14: default: break;
    }
    out += " of ";
    out += figure_descriptor(e->figure, ctx, true, false); // 0xb92f10
    out += " ";
    switch (e->selector) {
    case 0: out += "as a member of"; break;
    case 1: out += "as a former member of"; break;
    case 2: out += "into the mercenary service of"; break;
    case 3: out += "as a former mercenary of"; break;
    case 4: case 6: out = "by"; break; // original native assign, not append
    case 5: out += "as a former slave of"; break;
    case 7: out += "as a former prisoner of"; break;
    case 8: out += "as an enemy of"; break;
    case 9: out += "in the eyes of"; break;
    case 10: case 12: {
        figure *f = find_figure(e->figure);
        p = find_entity_position(e->entity, e->position);
        if (!f || !p) break;
        out += "to the position of ";
        if (f->sex == 0 && !p->name_female[0].empty()) out += p->name_female[0];
        else if (f->sex == 1 && !p->name_male[0].empty()) out += p->name_male[0];
        else out += p->name[0];
        out += " of";
        break;
    }
    case 13:
        p = find_entity_position(e->entity, e->position);
        if (p) { out += "as a "; out += p->squad[0]; out += " of"; }
        break;
    case 15: out += "for"; break;
    case 11: case 14: default: break;
    }
    out += " ";
    out += entity_descriptor(e->entity, ctx->flags); // 0xb92900
    out += " in ";
    append_date(out, e->year, e->tick);
}

// The complete RAW office occupies one string field. Native " of " and the
// organization are appended after that field; an office such as "captain of
// the guard" does not turn the later organization into an office territory.
// The selector-13 squad class is one RAW field too, without sex lookup. This
// is entity_position.squad[0] at +0x218, not spouse[0] (+0x158), and is not a
// player's custom squad.alias. An existing adapter comment calls variant 3
// "spouse", but its actual +0x218 read agrees with the native squad class.
// Invalid/missing position paths deliberately retain the same common suffix;
// the source reconstruction does not invent a missing office or event name.

===============================================================================
AGREEMENT-FORMED ROOT: COMPLETE 18-WAY INLINE BLOCK DISPATCH
Reference 0x2ad7f0..0x2afec3; Classic 0x2ab3b0..0x2ada83
Reference jump table 0x2afde4; Classic 0x2ad9a4.
===============================================================================

// Structured control-flow reconstruction. Inline labels below designate blocks
// in the complete paired all-agreement-subject-branches.asm sources, not new
// functions or an inferred title lookup. Every block ends at the same date tail.
void agreement_formed_subject(event *e, string &out, context *ctx) {
    agreement *a = find_agreement(e->agreement_id /* +0x28 */);
    if (!a || a->parties.empty() || a->elements.empty()) goto corrupt_fallback;
    element *el = a->elements[0]; // native reads +0x28 vector[0]
    if ((unsigned)el->type > 17) goto corrupt_fallback;
    switch (el->type) {
    case 0: goto joining_0x2af744;
    case 1: goto permanent_joining_0x2af206;
    case 2: goto residency_0x2af4f2;
    case 3: goto citizenship_0x2af630;
    case 4: goto parley_0x2af3ad;
    case 5: goto corrupt_action_0x2aeec6;
    case 6: goto theft_plot_0x2ae859;
    case 7: goto promise_0x2aeabc;
    case 8: goto assassination_0x2ae5ec;
    case 9: goto abduction_0x2ae37f;
    case 10: goto sabotage_0x2ae0bc;
    case 11: goto conspiracy_0x2ad98d;
    case 12: goto establish_building_0x2af9f9;
    case 13: goto infiltration_0x2adae0;
    case 14: goto frame_0x2adc39;
    case 15: goto induce_war_0x2adee4;
    case 16: goto service_request_0x2afb55;
    case 17: goto retrieve_request_0x2afc7d;
    }
corrupt_fallback:
    out += "the formation of a corrupt agreement";
date_tail: // 0x2ad8bf, also used by every successful branch
    out += " in ";
    append_date(out, e->year, e->tick);
}

// All subjects call native party getter 0xb9dc0 against agreement.parties.
// A missing required party contributes "an unknown party". Mixed party lists
// use 0xe2b80 and retain every entry with the native two/Oxford-list punctuation.
// The actual operands and conditional helper calls remain in paired assembly.
// These are the complete arm production families:
//  0 "the joining of " PARTY " with " PARTY + one purpose arm below.
//  1 "the permanent joining by " PARTY " of " PARTY [" to the living world"].
//  2 "the agreement between " PARTY " and " PARTY + one resident purpose.
//  3 "the agreement between " PARTY " and " PARTY [" and become a citizen of " SITE].
//  4 "the parley between " PARTY " and " PARTY.
//  5 "the passing of corruptly-obtained funds by " / "the embezzlement of" /
//    "the bribery of" PARTY + office/entity/influence/recipient/messenger arms.
//  6 "the plot of " PARTY " to steal " ARTIFACT + influence/messengers.
//  7 "the promise by " PARTY " to " PARTY + equality/position/entity arms.
//  8 "the plot of " PARTY " to assassinate " FIGURE + influence/messengers.
//  9 "the plot of " PARTY " to abduct " FIGURE + influence/messengers.
// 10 "the plot of " PARTY " to sabotage the activities of " ENTITY
//    [" at " SITE] + influence/messengers.
// 11 "the embezzlement conspiracy" / "the corruption conspiracy" /
//    "the bribery conspiracy" + " concocted by " all-parties.
// 12 "the agreement by " PARTY " to establish " BUILDING-CLASS " for " ENTITY.
// 13 "the plot of " PARTY " to infiltrate " ENTITY + influence.
// 14 "the plot of " PARTY " to frame " [FIGURE] " for " [CRIME]
//    " by fooling " [FIGURE] + influence.
// 15 "the plot of " PARTY " to induce a war of " [ENTITY] " upon " [ENTITY]
//    + influence.
// 16 "the request by " PARTY " that " PARTY " make an offer of service"
//    [" to " ENTITY].
// 17 "the request by " PARTY " that " PARTY " retrieve " ARTIFACT
//    [" from " SITE] [" for " PARTY].

// Joining's complete finite purpose dispatch (0x2af96a / 0x2af9af return to
// date_tail directly, preventing the guide branch from chaining multiple goals):
switch (joining.data[0]) {
case 0:  append(" to oust ", optional_entity, " from ", optional_site); break;
case 1:  append(" to live a life of adventure"); break;
case 2:
    append(" as a guide");
    if (joining.data[5] != -1) append(" to find ", figure(joining.data[5]));
    else if (joining.data[4] != -1) append(" to find ", identity(joining.data[4]));
    else if (joining.data[3] != -1) append(" to ", site(joining.data[3]));
    break;
case 23: append(" in order to be brought to safety"); break;
case 24: append(" to help rescue ", optional_figure); break;
case 39: append(" in bound service"); break;
case 42: append(" to entertain the world"); break;
default: break; // no purpose text; the main joining subject and date remain
}

// Residency purpose and optional site are independent native conditions:
switch (residency.data[0]) {
case 41: append(" to eradicate monsters"); break;
case 42: append(" to entertain the citizenry"); break;
case 43: append(" to work as a mercenary"); break;
case 44: append(" to study"); break;
default: break;
}
if (residency.data[3] != -1)
    append(" and become a resident of ", site(residency.data[3]));
if (citizenship.data[2] != -1)
    append(" and become a citizen of ", site(citizenship.data[2]));

// The promise's optional recipient does not acquire an unknown-party noun when
// different from the beneficiary; equal includes the case where both are null.
party *beneficiary = get_party(promise.data[0]);
party *promiser = get_party(promise.data[1]);
party *recipient = get_party(promise.data[2]);
append("the promise by ", required_party(promiser), " to ", required_party(beneficiary));
if (recipient == beneficiary) append(" of");
else { append(" to give "); if (recipient) append(party_name(recipient)); }
append(" a position");
if (promise.data[10] != -1) append(" in ", entity(promise.data[10]));
// Influence = party data[3]; via uses the complete messenger vector, not one ID.

// Frame's 19-entry crime table has a genuine empty default. Even with a missing
// target, crime or fooled actor, " to frame ", " for " and " by fooling " remain.
// Optional infiltration entity is data[2] != -1. Optional induce-war attacker
// and defender entities are independently data[2] != -1 and data[3] != -1.

===============================================================================
SHARED REASON + CIRCUMSTANCE HELPER: COMPLETE SELECTOR CONTROL FLOW
Reference 0xb5a6c0..0xb5bab1; Classic 0xb57700..0xb58af1
===============================================================================

// Native calling convention: out RCX; reason EDX; value/typed ID R8D;
// circumstance R9D; circumstance ID fifth stack argument; context sixth.
// Reasons and circumstances run independently. A reason does not consume the
// circumstance, and both retain a preceding separator when out is nonempty.
void append_history_adjuncts(string &out, int reason, int value,
                             int circumstance, int circumstance_id, context *ctx) {
    if (reason != -1) {
        if (!out.empty()) out += " ";
        if ((unsigned)reason <= 93) dispatch_reason(reason, value, out, ctx);
    }
    if (circumstance != -1) {
        if (!out.empty()) out += " ";
        if ((unsigned)circumstance <= 280)
            dispatch_circumstance(circumstance, circumstance_id, out, ctx);
    }
}
// Each local block named below is retained in shared-history-reasons.asm. This
// preserves all real selector numbers, including the numerous blank/default
// enum slots, instead of inventing a dense 26-element circumstance enumeration.

// The primary reason switch contains 94 arms (0..93). Its nested value switch
// contains 33 arms (0..32). The scholarly-interest switch uses value-61 plus
// byte remapping over 64 normalized slots. Circumstance uses byte remapping
// over 281 slots, including the repeated no-text destinations.
// Dynamic leaves remain typed: figure, entity, site, identity, artifact,
// scholarly topic, value wording, historical collection title. The collection
// leaf uses virtual +0x30 over all 18 concrete collection RTTI roots, not an
// unbounded English string. Rituals retain the prayer and temple suffix arms;
// owned-item/body and cosmic/value nuances are distinct original productions.

===============================================================================
ARTIFACT-COPY ROOT: ORIGINAL FLAG AND ALL UNCONDITIONAL QUALIFIERS
Reference 0xb8a150..0xb8a2cb
===============================================================================

void artifact_copied_subject(event *e, string &out, context *ctx) {
    out += "the acquisition of a copy of ";
    if (e->flags_44 & 1) out += "the original ";
    out += artifact_identity(e->artifact_28, ctx); // 0xb94400
    out += " from ";
    out += abstract_building(e->site_38, e->building_40, true, ctx->flags);
    out += " in "; out += site(e->site_38, ctx->flags);
    out += " of "; out += entity(e->entity_30, ctx->flags);
    out += " by "; out += entity(e->entity_2c, ctx->flags);
    out += " for ";
    out += abstract_building(e->site_34, e->building_3c, true, ctx->flags);
    out += " in "; out += site(e->site_34, ctx->flags);
    out += " in "; append_date(out, e->year, e->tick);
}
// The six source/destination helpers above are not guarded by -1. Their own
// native missing-object branches supply their established text boundaries.

===============================================================================
ARTIFACT-DESTROYED ROOT: ALL ACTOR/ENTITY/SITE ARMS AND THE COMMON DATE TAIL
Reference 0xb8ac80..0xb8ad98; Classic 0xb87cc0..0xb87dd8; native event type 87
===============================================================================

void artifact_destroyed_subject(event *e, string &out, context *ctx) {
    out += "the destruction of ";
    out += artifact_identity(e->artifact_28, ctx->flags);
    // Reference identity helper 0xb94400; Classic 0xb91440.
    if (e->destroyer_hf_30 != -1) {
        out += " by ";
        out += figure_descriptor(e->destroyer_hf_30, ctx, true, false);
        // Reference 0xb92f10; Classic 0xb8ff50.
        if (e->destroyer_entity_34 != -1) {
            out += " and ";
            out += entity_descriptor(e->destroyer_entity_34, ctx->flags);
        }
    } else if (e->destroyer_entity_34 != -1) {
        out += " by ";
        out += entity_descriptor(e->destroyer_entity_34, ctx->flags);
    }
    // Reference entity helper 0xb92900; Classic 0xb8f940.
    if (e->site_2c != -1) {
        out += " in ";
        out += site_descriptor(e->site_2c, ctx->flags);
        // Reference 0xb93930; Classic 0xb90970.
    }
    out += " in "; // always emitted, even when actors/site are absent
    append_date(out, e->year_08, e->tick_0c);
}

// artifact-destroyed-productions.tsv retains all eight independent HF/entity/
// site-presence combinations. date-productions.tsv retains all fourteen ordinary
// date productions and all three malformed-season defaults. The date tail is
// unconditional, so an unknown tick is YEAR alone rather than absent text.
// The current screenshot takes HF absent, entity absent, site present:
//   "the destruction of " ARTIFACT " in " SITE " in " DATE
// ARTIFACT's native identity is Yearlingfortunes; SITE is Floorburns; DATE is
// "the midspring of 102". The enclosing image-paragraph adds the artwork prefix,
// optional historical-collection suffix, and terminal ".  ". There is no reason
// to reinterpret ARTIFACT as a place or to let SITE absorb the final DATE.
// A raw sentence list cannot enumerate arbitrary names, save data, RAW/mod text,
// or numeric years. The finite branches plus their typed leaves are the source
// language. The paired complete event-source-call-closure files retain every
// reachable concrete RTTI root, each switch selector including empty defaults,
// literal operand, direct dependency, and explicit typed indirect edge.
